newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Costain sees improvement on year.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Costain sees improvement on year.

text.p: Costain Group, which clinched a last-ditch survival refinancing this summer, said it expected its full year results to be "considerably better" than last year, after reporting extended first half losses on Wednesday.

Despite interim profits plunging 19.2 million stg into the red from 10.4 million last year, Allan Lovell, chief executive, told Reuters that he was confident of much improved profitability, with all units expected to move ahead.
He cited a number of reasons for his confidence -- despite an interim report which said trading conditions remained little changed and saw losses deepen across all divisions.

First, construction turnover in the six months to June 30 had been "well below the trend". But he said the turnover position would improve significantly in the second half, predicting "over 300 million stg" in sales.
"This is a key issue," said Lovell. He added: "And it's not just the amount (of business) but the quality."
Costain now had four big projects, with a share worth 25 million stg apiece, at decent margins, he said.
He said the year end results would also be boosted by the fact that there "will not be any write-offs - this will make them hugely better." Underlying trading should also improve.
But despite his high hopes Lovell refused to be drawn on when the company will start paying dividends to investors again.
He said there was a timeframe he had in mind but "I'm not setting myself up as a hostage of fortune," he added.

The on-going saga of the effort to sell U.S. Coal continued into the second half. But Lovell told Reuters that talks were underway with an interested party. But he would not comment on when a sale could take place.

Commenting on future strategy, Costain said that its three biggest shareholders -- Intria of Malaysia, M.A. Kharafi and Sons of Kuwait and Raymond International of Saudi which own a total of 75 percent of shares -- were key to its plan to expand overseas business.
It saw these investors as a springboard into the South East Asia and Middle East markets, with their contacts helping Costain win better margin business -- particularly in Malaysia.
It expects Intria to help it gain small contracts in the next six months and a stake in a larger project next year.
Costain aims to have the largest proportion of its business stemming from overseas markets in the years ahead.
But Lovell refused to be drawn on the targets he has in mind and stressed the UK will remain an important market.

Commenting on the recent strained relations with investor Kharafi which launched a bitter attack on Costain earlier this summer over demands for another cash injection, Lovell said all differences had now been resolved.
